title: Viva Engage: advanced moderation permission for corporate communicators
summary: Hold: the briefing treats private-community access for theme moderation as undocumented, but Microsoft's AI summarization and theme extraction FAQ explicitly preserves users' existing content permissions. The roadmap facts, licensing threshold and listed control paths are supported; two minor corrections concern the Graph request-body note and checklist coverage.

claims.claim: The Corporate Communicator assignment route is Viva Engage admin center > Setup and configuration > Admin roles > Corporate communicator > Add user.

claims.claim: POST /v1.0/employeeExperience/roles/{engagementRoleId}/members assigns a Viva Engage role to a user, not the granular moderation permission.
claims.quote: Create a new engagementRoleMember object that assigns a Viva Engage role to a user. POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/employeeExperience/roles/a40473a5-0fb4-a250-e029-f6fe33d07733/members
claims.fix: Keep the call. Add to controls[1].note and the matching rendered note: 'The request body identifies the assignee through userId; Microsoft's HTTP example uses user@odata.bind.' The cited create-member reference documents userId in its request-body table and user@odata.bind in its example.

claims.claim: The Graph role assignment operation requires EngagementRole.ReadWrite.All.
claims.quote: Delegated (work or school account): EngagementRole.ReadWrite.All. Application: EngagementRole.ReadWrite.All.

claims.claim: The Graph Viva Engage API supports native-mode networks only.
claims.quote: The Viva Engage API in Microsoft Graph is only supported for Viva Engage networks in native mode. You can't use this API to manage legacy or external Viva Engage networks.

claims.claim: The Graph engagementRoleMember object describes a user-role association and its assignment date, without a granular moderation permission property.
claims.quote: Each role member links a predefined role to a specific user, and multiple users can be assigned to the same role. Properties: createdDateTime, id, userId. Relationships: user.

claims.claim: AI-related feature access management is reached through Viva Engage admin center > Setup & configuration > Manage analytics > Analytics settings > Feature access management.
claims.quote: Select the Setup & configuration tab, and select Manage analytics. Activate AI-related features from the Analytics settings page > Feature access management.

claims.claim: Add-VivaModuleFeaturePolicy with ModuleId, FeatureId, Name, IsFeatureEnabled $false and Everyone creates an organization-wide disabling policy for the specified feature.
claims.quote: Add-VivaModuleFeaturePolicy -ModuleId VivaInsights -FeatureId Reflection -Name DisableFeatureForAll -IsFeatureEnabled $false -Everyone. The FeatureId value is returned in the output of the cmdlet.

claims.claim: The Engage admin manages AI Summarization feature access.
claims.quote: AI Summarization | Yes | Engage admin | Viva Engage

claims.claim: AI Summarization supports network-wide, group and individual access policies.
claims.quote: Engage admins can create access policies in PowerShell to turn off AI summarization for the entire network, or for select groups and individuals.

claims.claim: AI Summarization supports a user opt-out enablement state.
claims.quote: Enabled with user opt out: Provides the same functionality as Enabled, except that users who have access to AI Summarization can turn it off for their user account through the setting in their personal analytics.

claims.claim: Disabling AI Summarization for the tenant stops processing and retroactively deletes tenant summarization history.
claims.quote: Stops all processing of Engage threads. If you disable AI summarization for the tenant, all history data in the tenant is retroactively deleted.

claims.claim: Learn advises a user or group enablement policy to prevent deletion of all summarization data.
claims.quote: To prevent deletion of all summarization data, create a user or group enablement policy or a tenant with a disability policy when you change the setting.

claims.claim: AI Summarization control changes generally take effect within 24 hours.
claims.quote: Changes to the AI summarization control generally take effect within 24 hours.

claims.claim: Theme creators reach theme action toggles through Communications dashboard > Advanced moderation > Add theme.
claims.quote: Go to Communications dashboard > Advanced moderation, and select Add theme. Enter a sensible category phrase in the Theme box. Enable the Auto-mute and Email notification toggles.

claims.claim: Theme matches can be reviewed in Advanced moderation > Detected conversations.
claims.quote: When you add new themes, ongoing conversations that match themes start to populate the Advanced moderation > Detected conversations table.

claims.claim: AI Summarization must remain enabled for the users whose conversations theme moderation processes.
claims.quote: Theme moderation is built on the Viva Engage AI Summarization service. By default, AI summarization is enabled and processes data across all users in your network unless you specify otherwise.
